name: Manoah and his wife
charge: Asking, how shall we order the child? and observing all that the angel commanded
summary: The angel of the Lord appeared to a barren woman of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, and told her she would bear a son who would be a Nazarite to God from the womb, with a rule laid on her as well: no wine, no strong drink, and nothing unclean. She told her husband, and Manoah prayed that the man of God would come again and teach them how to raise the child, and the Lord heard him. They offered a young goat on a rock, the angel rose in the flame, and they fell on their faces. His wife reasoned rightly: if the Lord had meant to kill them He would not have accepted an offering from them.
offenseFull: Israel did evil again in the Lord’s sight, and He gave them into the hand of the Philistines forty years. A man of Zorah of the family of Dan named Manoah had a wife who was barren (Judges 13:1-7). This is one of many places where our foremothers went through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready He enabled them to conceive; He settles the childless woman in her home as a happy mother of children (Psalms 113:9). Sisters who have tried for years should be patient, take comfort in the scriptures, and believe what the Bible says. The angel of the Lord told the woman she would conceive and bear a son, and laid the rule on her as well as on the child: no wine or strong drink, nothing unclean, and no razor on his head, because the child would be a Nazarite to

God from the womb and would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. Even in the womb he was to be kept pure. That is the vow set out in the law, the separation of a man or woman to the Lord, with nothing from the grapevine, seeds or skins, and no razor on the head while the hair grows long (Numbers 6:2-5). Understand the difference between a Nazarite and a Nazarene: Christ was a Nazarene because He was of the city of Nazareth, and He drank wine, which a Nazarite could not do. Samson was a Nazarite from birth, and so were Samuel and John the Baptist after him. The locks also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows that way.

The woman told her husband that a man of God had come to her, looking like an angel of God, very frightening. The popular pictures of angels as babies with smooth cheeks and little white wings do not match scripture at all; to see an angel of the Most High was terrifying, blazing like lightning in snow-white clothes (Matthew 28:3). Manoah prayed that the man of God would come again and teach them how to raise the child, and God heard him; the angel came again to the woman in the field, and she ran to fetch her husband (Judges 13:8-14). Manoah asked how the child should be raised, and the angel only repeated what he had already told the woman, that she must keep all of it. Their task was not to invent a manner of upbringing for an extraordinary child. It was to receive the instruction and keep it.
judgmentFull: Manoah tried to keep the angel and prepare a young goat for him; the angel refused to eat, and said that if they offered a burnt offering it must be to the Lord, for Manoah did not know he was an angel of the Lord (Judges 13:15-25). The angel knew Manoah might try to offer it to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering where it belonged. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God, which is why the letters warn against being cheated by false humility and the worship of angels (Colossians 2:18), and why, when John fell at the angel’s feet to worship, the angel stopped him, calling himself a fellow servant, and told him to worship God (Revelation 22:8-9). Manoah asked his name, and the angel asked why he wanted to know, since it was secret.

Manoah offered a young goat with a grain offering on a rock to the Lord, and the angel did a wonder: as the flame went up from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the Lord rose in the flame and was gone, and Manoah and his wife fell face down to the ground (Judges 13:19-23). Angels are made of that fire; they have bodies, they walk, they eat, they come and go, and one of them can take the flame off an altar and rise in it. Manoah said they would surely die, because they had seen God. The contradictors point to this, since the Bible says no man has seen God; but the word there is Elohim, which is plural and speaks of heavenly beings. They saw an angel, not the Most High; no flesh can look upon Him, and the furthest anybody got was Moses seeing His back. His wife reasoned rightly: if the Lord had wanted to kill them He would not have accepted their offerings or shown them all these things. She bore a son and named him Samson, the child grew and the Lord blessed him, and the Spirit of the Lord began to stir him in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.

text.text: And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord; and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bare not.
And the angel of the Lord appeared unto the woman, and said unto her, Behold now, thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.
Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing:

For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.

Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, A man of God came unto me, and his countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible: but I asked him not whence he was, neither told he me his name:

But he said unto me, Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink, neither eat any unclean thing: for the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death.
He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When either man or woman shall separate themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the Lord:
He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink, and shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of strong drink, neither shall he drink any liquor of grapes, nor eat moist grapes, or dried.
All the days of his separation shall he eat nothing that is made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk.

All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.
His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow:
Then Manoah intreated the Lord, and said, O my Lord, let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us, and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born.
And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband was not with her.
And the woman made haste, and ran, and shewed her husband, and said unto him, Behold, the man hath appeared unto me, that came unto me the other day.
And Manoah arose, and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said unto him, Art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? And he said, I am.
And Manoah said, Now let thy words come to pass. How shall we order the child, and how shall we do unto him?
And the angel of the Lord said unto Manoah, Of all that I said unto the woman let her beware.
She may not eat of any thing that cometh of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing: all that I commanded her let her observe.
And Manoah said unto the angel of the Lord, I pray thee, let us detain thee, until we shall have made ready a kid for thee.

And the angel of the Lord said unto Manoah, Though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread: and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord. For Manoah knew not that he was an angel of the Lord.
And Manoah said unto the angel of the Lord, What is thy name, that when thy sayings come to pass we may do thee honour?
And the angel of the Lord said unto him, Why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret?
So Manoah took a kid with a meat offering, and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord: and the angel did wondrously; and Manoah and his wife looked on.

For it came to pass, when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, that the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife looked on it, and fell on their faces to the ground.
But the angel of the Lord did no more appear to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord.
And Manoah said unto his wife, We shall surely die, because we have seen God.

But his wife said unto him, If the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things, nor would as at this time have told us such things as these.
And the woman bare a son, and called his name Samson: and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him.
And the Spirit of the Lord began to move him at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.
Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,
And I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.
Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.
So Manoah took a kid with a meat offering, and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord: and the angel did wondrously; and Manoah and his wife looked on.

For it came to pass, when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, that the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife looked on it, and fell on their faces to the ground.
But the angel of the Lord did no more appear to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord.

But his wife said unto him, If the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things, nor would as at this time have told us such things as these.

Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing:
